summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and severe neuropathic pain in the setting of type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis. She had not completed her dialysis the night before admission and presented with low sodium and poor oral intake. Workup showed no infection, with negative blood and peritoneal cultures. A gastric emptying study confirmed moderate to severe gastroparesis. She was treated with IV fluids, ondansetron, and erythromycin for gastroparesis, which improved over several days. For neuropathic pain and fibromyalgia, pregabalin was started and nortriptyline added, with gabapentin discontinued. She tolerated a gradual return to oral intake, had no emesis for over 48 hours, and was ambulating independently at discharge. She was discharged home with new prescriptions for pregabalin and nortriptyline, instructions to continue domperidone from her personal supply, and plans for outpatient EGD with botox injection. Regular EKG monitoring was recommended due to QT-prolonging medications.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
